label: MORNING BRIEF

stories.title: Lira homes marked for demolition
stories.story: Dozens of Lira homes are marked as the Tororo–Gulu line reaches 75%. MPs say URC is missing titles for about 62 of its 286 plots.
stories.you: It’s not just Kampala. Check the railway reserve before you list a plot near the line.

stories.title: MPs to check 2,313 Asian properties
stories.story: MPs ordered checks on 2,313 properties left by Asians expelled in 1972. The Custodian Board earns from only five of the 2,515 on its list.
stories.you: Old building in town? Ask if it’s Custodian Board property before you let or sell it.

stories.title: Wakiso farmers warn of land grabs
stories.story: At a district farm show, Wakiso farmers named land grabbing a major problem. Leaders under LC5 chairman Ian Kyeyune say they have a plan to fight it.
stories.you: Selling farmland in Wakiso? Find out who is using the land before your client pays.

stories.title: Bonds pay more than property
stories.story: Fund managers say property returns go as high as 13%. Ten-year government bonds pay 15.2% after tax. No developer has started a REIT.
stories.you: Investors compare returns. Show buyers the rent a property earns, not just its price.

stories.title: An agency teams up with a bank
stories.story: Bakaima Real Estate Agents handed over a land title at Bujuuko Estate for Housing Finance Bank’s Zimba Challenge home. 164 people pitched ideas.
stories.you: Banks want partners. Pitch your estates to a bank — its customers need homes.
